name: Raw iron (iron ore)
abstraction: One item is treated as a 100 g laboratory sample (a game convention; Minecraft items have no defined mass). Modelled as hematite (Fe₂O₃) with quartz gangue; real iron ores vary widely.
description: Ore is rock containing enough of a metal compound to be worth extracting. It is not pure iron: the iron is chemically combined with oxygen.

name: Iron ingot
abstraction: One item is treated as a 100 g laboratory sample (a game convention; Minecraft items have no defined mass). Treated as pure iron; real wrought iron and steel contain small amounts of carbon and other elements.
description: A refined metal produced by removing oxygen from iron ore (reduction).

name: Iron nugget
abstraction: One nugget is one ninth of a 100 g ingot.
description: A small piece of refined iron.

name: Raw copper (copper ore)
abstraction: One item is treated as a 100 g laboratory sample (a game convention; Minecraft items have no defined mass). Modelled as chalcopyrite (CuFeS₂) with quartz gangue.
description: Most copper is mined as sulfide minerals such as chalcopyrite, not as metal.

name: Copper ingot
abstraction: One item is treated as a 100 g laboratory sample (a game convention; Minecraft items have no defined mass). Treated as pure copper.
description: Refined copper, an excellent electrical conductor.

name: Raw gold (gold ore)
abstraction: One item is treated as a 100 g laboratory sample (a game convention; Minecraft items have no defined mass). Modelled as native gold in quartz — a very rich ore compared with real deposits, where gold is often measured in grams per tonne.
description: Gold occurs as native metal, commonly in quartz veins.

name: Gold ingot
abstraction: One item is treated as a 100 g laboratory sample (a game convention; Minecraft items have no defined mass). Treated as pure gold.
description: Refined gold. Its very high density makes it easy to tell apart from other yellow metals.

name: Coal
abstraction: One item is treated as a 100 g laboratory sample (a game convention; Minecraft items have no defined mass). Real coal contains hydrocarbons, water, sulfur and mineral ash; it is modelled as 85 % carbon plus silicate ash. Density is that of typical bituminous coal (1.3–1.4 g/cm³), not of the simplified components.
description: A sedimentary rock formed from ancient plant material. Burning its carbon releases about 394 kJ per mole of carbon.

name: Charcoal
abstraction: One item is treated as a 100 g laboratory sample (a game convention; Minecraft items have no defined mass). Charcoal is very porous, so its bulk density (≈0.4 g/cm³) is far below that of solid carbon; displacement measurements of porous samples are unreliable.
description: Made by heating wood without enough air to burn it, driving off water and volatile compounds.

name: Diamond
abstraction: One item is treated as a 100 g laboratory sample (a game convention; Minecraft items have no defined mass). Real gem diamonds weigh far less than 100 g.
description: Pure carbon in a rigid tetrahedral network.

name: Sand
abstraction: One item is treated as a 100 g laboratory sample (a game convention; Minecraft items have no defined mass). Modelled as pure quartz sand. The density is that of the grains; loose sand has a bulk density of about 1.6 g/cm³ because of the air between grains.
description: Small grains of weathered rock, mostly quartz.

name: Nether quartz
abstraction: One item is treated as a 100 g laboratory sample (a game convention; Minecraft items have no defined mass). Minecraft's nether quartz is treated as ordinary quartz.
description: Crystalline silicon dioxide.

name: Amethyst
abstraction: One item is treated as a 100 g laboratory sample (a game convention; Minecraft items have no defined mass). Amethyst is quartz coloured purple by traces of iron and natural irradiation; the traces are ignored.
description: A purple variety of quartz.

name: Flint
abstraction: One item is treated as a 100 g laboratory sample (a game convention; Minecraft items have no defined mass). Flint is microcrystalline quartz with small amounts of water and impurities.
description: A hard rock that breaks with sharp edges, used for early stone tools.

name: Calcite
abstraction: One item is treated as a 100 g laboratory sample (a game convention; Minecraft items have no defined mass).
description: Crystalline calcium carbonate; it fizzes in acid and splits light into two images (double refraction).

name: Dripstone
abstraction: One item is treated as a 100 g laboratory sample (a game convention; Minecraft items have no defined mass). Real speleothems are mostly calcite deposited from dripping water.
description: Cave formations deposited from water saturated with calcium carbonate.

name: Clay
abstraction: One item is treated as a 100 g laboratory sample (a game convention; Minecraft items have no defined mass). Clay is a mixture of minerals; kaolinite is used as a representative.
description: Fine-grained mineral particles that become plastic when wet and hard when fired.

name: Glass
abstraction: One item is treated as a 100 g laboratory sample (a game convention; Minecraft items have no defined mass). Modelled as soda-lime glass.
description: An amorphous solid made by melting sand with sodium and calcium compounds and cooling it before crystals can form.

name: Obsidian
abstraction: One item is treated as a 100 g laboratory sample (a game convention; Minecraft items have no defined mass). Obsidian is volcanic glass; this is a typical rhyolitic composition (oxide basis).
description: Lava that cooled so quickly that no crystals formed.

name: Emerald
abstraction: One item is treated as a 100 g laboratory sample (a game convention; Minecraft items have no defined mass). Trace chromium/vanadium colourants are ignored.
description: A green gem variety of the mineral beryl.

name: Bone meal
abstraction: One item is treated as a 100 g laboratory sample (a game convention; Minecraft items have no defined mass). Only the mineral part of bone is modelled; real bone meal also contains protein and water.
description: Ground bone, rich in calcium phosphate.

name: Sugar
abstraction: One item is treated as a 100 g laboratory sample (a game convention; Minecraft items have no defined mass).
description: Crystalline sucrose, a molecular compound.

name: Ice
abstraction: One item is treated as a 100 g laboratory sample (a game convention; Minecraft items have no defined mass).
description: Solid water. It floats because it is less dense than liquid water.

name: Redstone dust
abstraction: Redstone is a fictional Minecraft material with no real-world composition. Scientia treats it only as a fictional signal conductor and never assigns it a chemical identity.
description: A fictional material. Scientia's circuits model real electricity, and redstone signals can switch them.

name: Salt crystals
abstraction: One item is a 10 g reagent portion.
description: Sodium chloride recovered by evaporating or distilling seawater.

name: Quicklime
abstraction: One item is a 10 g reagent portion.
description: Calcium oxide made by strongly heating calcium carbonate.

name: Slaked lime
abstraction: One item is a 10 g reagent portion.
description: Calcium hydroxide made by adding water to quicklime.

name: Calcite powder
abstraction: One item is a 10 g reagent portion. Grinding is a physical change: the powder is still calcium carbonate.
description: Finely ground calcite; the larger surface area makes it react faster.

name: Copper(II) oxide powder
abstraction: One item is a 10 g reagent portion.
description: Black copper(II) oxide formed by heating copper in air.
